variables.claim_asserts: Amphibians are absent as native inhabitants of oceanic islands.
variables.test_measures: GBIF Amphibia occurrences in 41 pre-registered oceanic island units, using at least 10 records and at least 95% of global records within a unit as an endemism-based proxy for native status.

modality.note: GBIF occurrence records can establish island presence, while near-endemism is a conservative proxy for nativeness rather than a direct native/introduced-status field.

assumptions.note: A species overwhelmingly recorded within an island unit is reasonable sufficient evidence of native presence; this criterion favors specificity and may miss native non-endemics.

scope.claim_scope: Native amphibians on oceanic islands generally.
scope.test_scope: Forty-one pre-registered oceanic island units with GBIF data, detecting only species meeting a conservative endemism threshold.

reasons: The Fiji, Palau, and São Tomé endemic amphibian records are directly relevant counterexamples to native absence.
The interpretation explicitly declares the at-least-10-record and at-least-95%-inside-unit endemism criterion as a conservative native-status proxy.
Sampling 41 island units and detecting only near-endemics narrows the global claim, although that narrowing cannot manufacture the positive counterexamples.
what_would_change_it: Use a comprehensive global oceanic-island inventory with authoritative species-level native, introduced, and uncertain status instead of inferring nativeness only from endemism.
